title: Alcaraz Gets His Revenge to Win First Paris Masters Title
summary:
Sixty days. That is how long Carlos Alcaraz waited for his rematch with Ben Shelton. Back in September, Alcaraz's comeback tournament ended in a late-night, five-set epic at the US Open. Shelton won that one. On Sunday in Paris, Alcaraz got even. The 23-year-old Spaniard beat world number four Shelton 7-6 (7-5), 7-5 to win his first Paris Masters title. It was a tense final, and Alcaraz had to dig deep from the very start. In the opening set, he saved all six break points against him, refusing to let Shelton break through. Then, trailing 4-3 in the tie-break, he won four of the final five points to steal the set. Shelton struck first in the second set, breaking Alcaraz in his third service game. But with Shelton serving for a 5-3 lead, Alcaraz hit back. Moments later, he pointed to his ear, asking the crowd for more noise, and even danced to the music in the stadium during the change of ends. He closed out the title on a second match point, winning five of the final six games.

'It's something I've been chasing for a long time,' Alcaraz said. 'Today was one of the toughest challenges we have in tennis right now, facing Ben.' The win was special because of the road back. Alcaraz had spent four months out with a wrist injury before returning at the US Open. Since that loss to Shelton, he has won three titles and lost only once in 17 matches.

The Paris crown is his ninth ATP Masters 1000 title overall, and he has now won seven of the nine Masters 1000 events. Only Canada and Shanghai remain. Next up is the ATP Finals in Turin, where the seven-time major winner arrives on a nine-match winning streak after also triumphing in Vienna.
why_it_matters: Comebacks take patience: Alcaraz shows that losing to the same opponent can be the start of a strong run back, and that saving your best tennis for the biggest points can turn a match around.
